cases.text: The mobile client team wants to parse trickplay.json's on-disk fields directly instead of waiting on a playbackInfo trickplay manifest, since internal/genassets already emits camelCase JSON. Before I greenlight reading that file as the client contract, confirm whether that's actually still true today, and if not, what supersedes it.
cases.rationale: internal/genassets/genassets.go's TrickplayManifest struct comment still literally says "the JSON index clients consume", citing the now-superseded ADR-0033 §6 — but ADR-0187 Decision 4 explicitly demotes trickplay.json to an internal artifact and moves the client contract to the normalized playbackInfo.trickplay field. This is the authority-over-naming trap: the code's own naming and comment argue the opposite of the governing decision.

ground_truth.contains: at the `playbackInfo` boundary and are no longer a client-facing contract.

cases.text: We're considering shortening the Stream Token max lifetime from 7 days to reduce the exposure window after a credential compromise. Before changing the constant, show me every place in the codebase that assumes today's MaxStreamTokenTTL value, especially any invalidation-retention floor derived from it.
cases.rationale: MaxStreamTokenTTL is a single constant in internal/streamtoken with several independent downstream consumers: the compat-refusal invalidation retention floor wired in internal/server, and the same durability invariant re-checked separately in internal/capabilities and internal/conformance. An impact query must surface all of them, not just the definition site, or a change would silently violate the durability invariant in an unreviewed package.

cases.text: Podcast episodes are getting inserted ads classified correctly, but a listener reported that a host-read sponsor segment got auto-skipped too. Show me where the audio-ad calibration decides whether a detected segment is safe to admit, and confirm host-read segments are excluded from auto-apply even at high classifier confidence.
cases.rationale: ADR-0193 stores the inserted-vs-host-read distinction as an internal flavor, never a public marker kind, and internal/skipdetect/podcast_ad.go's admits() hard-excludes FlavorHostRead regardless of confidence, proven by TestAudioAdHostReadNeverAdmitted. The general skip-segment detector (skipdetect.go) handles an unrelated intro/recap/credits vocabulary and must not be conflated with podcast ad classification despite living in the same package.

ground_truth.contains: the marker means to a viewer — so it is stored as an internal **flavor** (`inserted` | `host-read`)

cases.text: We want to ship a first-party Kubernetes Helm chart for Beamfall Core with a HorizontalPodAutoscaler so our EKS-hosted deployment can autoscale transcode worker pods under load. Point me at the existing Helm chart or Kubernetes manifests so I can add the HPA alongside them.
cases.rationale: Beamfall's packaging surface is Docker Compose, TrueNAS, and Unraid only (packaging/compose, packaging/truenas, packaging/unraid); there is no Kubernetes manifest, Helm chart, or autoscaler definition anywhere in the tree, and ADR-0013 (operations and packaging) does not describe an elastic, pod-based deployment model. A retrieval tool must abstain rather than invent a plausible-looking chart location.
